question:
How do i unlink the GitHub Slack Integration just from DMs?
Select Topic Area
Question
The github bot integration on the Slack has a link button in its DM but does not have an unlink slash command. I've searched its settings for an hour with no luck.
How do i stop the GitHub bot from tagging my slack username in places, or better yet, just unlink the bot from my personal account, but still keep it in the slack workspace and all its slack channels.
predicted_answer: Use `/github signout` in the GitHub app DM. GitHub Docs says this command “disconnects your GitHub account from your Slack user,” and the app stays installed in the workspace because installation is separate from your personal connection. If you only want to stop being mentioned in Slack notifications, remove the repo notifications you subscribed to with `/github unsubscribe OWNER/REPO ...`; GitHub Docs says you will be mentioned in Slack when repository events reference you, such as assignment or a comment mention.

arguments.pattern: ^##|unsubscribe|notifications are enabled by default|remove an existing label filter

Question
I have enrolled to the copilot annual subscription. Can I cancel the subscription while it is available, and will I get back the remaining payment?
predicted_answer: You can cancel a Copilot plan at any time, but GitHub says you keep access until the billing cycle ends and are then downgraded to Copilot Free. The docs do not say that the unused portion of an annual payment is refunded, so I could not confirm any remaining-payment refund from the documentation.

question:
Does a Rest API endpoint exist for enabling the dependency graph on a per repo basis?
Select Topic Area
Question
I'm trying to enable the dependency graph on a per repo basis, rather then at a global org or enterprise level. I can't seem to see it in the repo settings when I call is this not possible via the rest API? Thanks!
predicted_answer: No documented REST endpoint exists for turning the dependency graph on per repository. The REST dependency-graph docs only cover dependency review, dependency submission, and SBOMs, while the enabling guide says the dependency graph is enabled for a repository via repository settings and separately mentions bulk enablement for user or organization scopes, not a repo-toggle REST API.

arguments.pattern: enable dependency graph for a repository

question:
Invalid secret, github-token is not defined in the referenced workflow I have the following GitHub Action setup for reuse: github.com mdn/workflows/blob/d971cc3696bf46ae32617e058393e45cec55ff85/.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml 
name: auto-merge
on: [workflow_call]
jobs:
auto-merge:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
- uses: actions/checkout@v2
- uses: ahmadnassri/action-dependabot-auto-merge@v2
with:
target: minor
github-token: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN }}
I am reusing it here: mdn-minimalist/auto-merge.yml at 4c2fd5a9fe02c844788001064d72d98dc2ef801b · mdn/mdn-minimalist · GitHub
When the action on mdn-minimalist is run, I get the following error:
Invalid secret, github-token is not defined in the referenced workflow
I am kinda stumped as it definitely looks to be defined in the referenced workflow. Any ideas? Is there a naming convention that I am missing? Thing is, the auto-merge action expects a github-token property so, I cannot simply name it token. Thank you in advance.
predicted_answer: `jobs.<job_id>.secrets` in the calling workflow must use secret names that are defined by `on.workflow_call.secrets` in the reusable workflow. GitHub Docs says the secret identifier in the caller "must match the names defined in the called workflow"; if you want to pass `github-token`, the reusable workflow must declare `on.workflow_call.secrets.github-token` (or use `secrets: inherit` to pass all caller secrets). Your current reusable workflow only passes `with: github-token: ...` to the action, but it does not define a reusable-workflow secret named `github-token`, so the caller fails validation.

arguments.pattern: github-token is not defined in the referenced workflow|referenced workflow|workflow_call|secrets: inherit
Invalid secret|not defined in the referenced workflow|referenced workflow

question:
Changing "Workflow permissions" to "Read and write"
Hello.
In my personal account I could successfully change the "Workflow permissions" from "Read" to "Read and write" (under Repo -> Settings -> Actions/General).
I just created a trial Enterprise. There, at organization or repo level, I cannot make the same change: the option "Read and write" is disabled with the message "Repository administrators will only be able to change the default permissions to a more restrictive setting".
How can I ensure to assign also write permissions to the workflows in my organizational repos?
Thank you
Stefano
predicted_answer: You cannot make “Read and write” the default at the organization/repository level if the enterprise/org policy is set to the more restrictive default. GitHub Docs says the default permissions can be configured in organization settings, but if the org has a more restrictive default, that option is selected in the repository settings and the permissive option is disabled. For enterprise/org defaults, the docs also say the more permissive setting cannot be chosen as the default for individual organizations or repositories. To grant write access, set the `permissions` key in the specific workflow file for the jobs that need it.

arguments.pattern: workflow permissions|Read and write|default permissions|repository administrators
workflow permissions|Read and write|default permissions|repository administrators
workflow permissions|Read and write|default permissions|repository administrators
You can set the default permissions for the `GITHUB_TOKEN`
The default permissions can also be configured in the organization settings
Created on or after February 2, 2023|more permissive setting cannot be chosen as the default for individual organizations or repositories
Anyone with write access to a repository can still modify the permissions granted to the `GITHUB_TOKEN` for a specific workflow, by editing the `permissions` key in the workflow file
